siblings.title: Eat Penang: A Street-Food Pilgrim's Field Guide to George Town & Beyond
siblings.summary: Penang's hawker legends, Michelin Bib stalls, kopitiams and one-star Nyonya, mapped by neighbourhood with EUR prices and closing days.

siblings.title: Sleep — Penang: Heritage Shophouses, Colonial Grandes Dames & Hill Retreats
siblings.summary: Where a couple should sleep in George Town and beyond — restored shophouses, the Blue Mansion, the E&O, design conversions, beach character at Batu Ferringhi and a Thai-rice-barn hill retreat, with EUR price bands.

siblings.title: Do — Penang: semi-adventurous activities & day-trips from George Town
siblings.summary: What to actually do around Penang on a first visit: Penang Hill + The Habitat canopy walks, national-park jungle-and-beach treks, Balik Pulau cycling, kayaking, island snorkelling and the street-art trail, each rated for difficulty, time and euro cost.

siblings.title: See Penang: The Unmissable Icons of George Town & Beyond
siblings.summary: First-timer's guide to Penang's must-see icons: George Town's UNESCO core, street art, clan houses, jetties, temples and Penang Hill, with 2026 hours, prices and booking lead times.

siblings.title: Offbeat Penang: Vipers, Ghost Tunnels, Pig-Blood Noodles and a Mosque on Stilts
siblings.summary: Twenty-odd weird, eerie and unexpected Penang finds a first-timer walks straight past — live pit vipers, the most haunted tunnels in Asia, carnivorous gardens, vanishing trades and pig-blood noodles.

siblings.title: Culture in Penang: A First-Timer's Guide to Museums, Festivals & Crafts
siblings.summary: When to come for Penang's festivals, which museums and art spaces are worth it, and the heritage crafts you can try yourself in George Town.

siblings.title: Around & Day-Trips: Getting In, Out and About Penang
siblings.summary: How a couple based in George Town arrives, leaves and explores Penang — hops from the Cameron Highlands/KL, onward to Langkawi, local transport, and the day-trip orbit, with times and euro costs.

sources.title: Siam Road Char Koay Teow — MICHELIN Guide
sources.claim: Siam Road Char Koay Teow is a charcoal-wok Michelin Bib Gourmand stall, a plate ~RM8-11 (≈€2), with long weekend queues.

sources.title: Air Itam Laksa, Penang
sources.claim: Air Itam assam laksa, sold at the foot of Kek Lok Si, is the pilgrimage bowl of sour mackerel-tamarind noodles (~RM7).

sources.title: Gurney Drive Hawker Centre
sources.claim: Gurney Drive Hawker Centre is Penang's best-known one-stop evening grazing ground for the iconic hawker dishes.

sources.title: Melaka and George Town — UNESCO World Heritage
sources.claim: George Town was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2008 for 500 years of Straits trading culture.

sources.title: Penang Street Art Guide
sources.claim: George Town's Ernest Zacharevic murals and wrought-iron caricatures are a free, walkable open-air art trail.

sources.title: Leong San Tong Khoo Kongsi
sources.claim: Leong San Tong Khoo Kongsi is George Town's most ornate Chinese clan house, open 9:00-17:00, RM15 (≈€3).

sources.title: Clan Jetties of Penang
sources.claim: Chew Jetty is the largest of the lived-in stilt-village clan jetties on Weld Quay, free to walk (donations).

sources.title: Penang Hill — Tickets
sources.claim: The Penang Hill funicular runs 06:30-23:00; standard return is RM40 (≈€8), Fast Lane RM80.

sources.title: The Habitat Penang Hill
sources.claim: The Habitat on Penang Hill offers paved canopy/treetop walkways and guided nature walks, entry from ~RM52-60 (≈€10-13).

sources.title: Kek Lok Si Temple
sources.claim: Kek Lok Si, Malaysia's largest Buddhist temple, has free grounds (8:30-17:30); the inclined lift and pagoda carry small fees.

sources.title: The Blue Mansion — Rooms
sources.claim: The indigo Cheong Fatt Tze (Blue) Mansion is an award-winning UNESCO restoration with only 18 rooms to stay in (~€130-280).

sources.title: Best Time to Visit Penang
sources.claim: Best time to visit Penang is the dry window mid-November to mid-February, avoiding the hotter April-August.

sources.title: Best Time to Visit Penang — onpenang
sources.claim: Penang's wetter monsoon runs roughly May-October, with rain usually in short bursts rather than all-day washouts.

sources.title: Penang Durian Season Calendar
sources.claim: Penang's main durian season peaks June-August with the best volume, variety and prices.

sources.title: EUR to MYR Rate — Wise
sources.claim: The mid-2026 mid-market rate is approximately €1 = RM4.7.

sources.title: Butterworth to Penang Island Ferry
sources.claim: The RapidFerry from Butterworth to George Town runs ~06:30-23:00 every 20-30 min, a 10-15 min crossing, RM2 (≈€0.45), cashless.

sources.title: Cameron Highlands to Penang — Rome2Rio
sources.claim: A direct coach from the Cameron Highlands to Penang takes about 4.5-5 hours, running many times daily, from ~RM32 (≈€7).

sources.title: Kuala Lumpur to Penang by Train
sources.claim: From KL, the scenic option is the KTMB ETS train to Butterworth (~3h35-4h20) then the ferry to George Town.

sources.title: George Town Free CAT Bus
sources.claim: The free CAT shuttle loops George Town's heritage sights 06:00-23:45 every 10-15 minutes.

sources.title: Pinang Peranakan Mansion
sources.claim: The Pinang Peranakan Mansion is open 9:30-17:00 with admission around RM20-25 (≈€4-5).

sources.title: Penang National Park Guide
sources.claim: The Penang National Park trek to Monkey Beach is ~1.5h each way, signposted and guide-free; the park's 250m canopy walkway is closed.

sources.title: Explore Balik Pulau
sources.claim: Guided Balik Pulau countryside cycling tours run through durian orchards and kampungs (easy, half-day, ~€30).

sources.title: Penang Snake Temple
sources.claim: The Snake Temple near the airport keeps live, free-roaming venomous Wagler's pit vipers; entrance is free.

sources.title: Penang to Langkawi
sources.claim: There is no reliable direct Penang-Langkawi ferry since 2020; flying (20 min, from ~RM60/€13) is the safe onward choice.

sources.title: The Habitat Penang Hill — notice
sources.claim: The Habitat's Curtis Crest Tree Top Walk is under maintenance from 13 May 2026, with some areas temporarily closed.

sources.title: Penang State Museum to reopen — The Star
sources.claim: The Penang State Museum on Farquhar Street is in a RM20m restoration (slated to reopen end-2025); confirm before going.

sources.title: Thaipusam Festival Malaysia
sources.claim: Thaipusam 2026 falls on Feb 2; Penang's Waterfall Temple hosts the grandest silver-chariot and kavadi procession.

sources.title: George Town Festival 2026
sources.claim: The George Town Festival runs Aug 1-9, 2026 with 40+ events, 80% of them free.

sources.title: The Blue Mansion — Daily Tours
sources.claim: The Blue Mansion runs 45-min guided tours at 11:00 and 15:30 (RM25, max 24 people) that sell out; book ahead.
